opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: Maximum grants: New Projects and Commissions £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications £5,000; Long-Term Research £20,000; Research and Travel £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research categories); individuals who are sculpture historians, academics and conservators (Research and Travel category). Applications not accepted from individuals independently wishing to create/inform/develop/research their own practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and research expanding appreciation of sculpture. Funds exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications, and collection development through acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing and display. Applications considered four times per year. Autumn round currently open, closing 1 September, for projects starting no sooner than 1 January 2027.

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation: UK up to £600; Europe up to £700; Rest of world up to £1,000. Accommodation provided in Leeds or Hertfordshire.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics or curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for longer six-week Senior Fellowships.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute's research facilities in Leeds or Hertfordshire (Studios & Gardens for Henry Moore-specific research), including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Applications are currently closed for 2026/27; the next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: £250 cash prize for BA dissertation and £250 for MA dissertation; winners also receive Henry Moore Institute publications to the cover value of £50.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: BA and MA students of all disciplines at UK universities, for a dissertation submitted within the past academic year relating directly to sculpture.
opportunities.summary: Each year two prizes are awarded for extended pieces of writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. Submissions for the 2026 prize will open in autumn.
